requirements.requirement: On node1, new interactive login sessions use a persistent default umask of 027.
requirements.summary: A root-owned, mode-0644 profile script sets umask 027 and Alpine's global profile sources profile.d scripts. Fresh interactive login shells directly reported 0027 and created files/directories with modes 0640/0750. The same configuration and behavior were observed after restart.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied. Direct configuration and behavioral checks establish umask 027 for new interactive login shells, including correct derived file and directory modes. The node-restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and observed unavailability, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered SSH, configuration, and umask behavior.
limitations: The interactive-session checks used a local root /bin/sh -lic shell rather than an authenticated SSH login or multiple user accounts, although they directly exercised an interactive login shell through the global profile path.

The lifecycle collector's failed-service probe was unsupported because it checks systemd on Alpine; direct OpenRC sshd status, listening-port, and SSH-banner checks nevertheless demonstrated relevant service recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material mutations had clear roles: installing the profile setting, bounded behavioral tests whose temporary objects were removed, and the required restart protocol. The only unnecessary retained residue was /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present afterward; it was not cleaned up. No new exposure, package damage, or conflicting service state was observed.
